Application Materials.content:
As part of your application, you must provide the following supporting documents:
- **Your official transcript.** Please read UCL’s guide on [getting your academic transcript](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/getting-your-academic-transcript "Getting your academic transcript"). Sending documents that cannot be accepted will delay your application being processed.
- **A personal statement.** UCL’s [personal statement guidance](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/writing-your-personal-statement "Writing your personal statement") offers advice on writing an effective personal statement.
- If you need a visa to study at UCL you will need to provide a copy of your current **passport**. If you do not have a valid passport, you can complete UCL’s Missing passport document and provide your passport later.
- Some courses require additional documents as part of your application; full details can be found on UCL’s [additional course requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/degree-types/courses-additional-requirements "Courses with additional requirements") page.
- If you meet UCL’s [English language requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/english-language-requirements "English Language requirements") using a UCL-recognised test, you should upload your official test report form or qualification. If you cannot provide this evidence when you submit your application, your application will still be considered.
The number of references needed to support your application can be found on the prospectus page for your course. You should read UCL’s guidance on [selecting your reference](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/selecting-your-references "Selecting your references") and contact your nominated referee(s) before starting your application to check they can provide a reference for you.
Do **not** password-protect or encrypt files. Before submitting, make sure you have uploaded the correct version of each supporting document, and that your official transcripts clearly show your name, your institution, and a list of your modules and any grades you have received. You cannot replace or add additional documents once you have submitted your application. UCL also asks applicants to provide accurate details of any work experience or previous employment either in the employment section or as part of an uploaded CV, and to upload any compulsory supporting documents required for the course to proceed.

Interview Requirements.content: Only a small number of UCL courses ask applicants to complete an interview or test as part of their application. If UCL needs you to do this, someone from the relevant academic department will contact you with further details. If you have any questions you should respond to the sender of the email. If you do not receive an invitation to an interview or test, this means that UCL will consider your application only on the information in your application and (where applicable) your references.

Application Deadlines.content:
- Programme starts **September 2026**.
- Applications accepted for applicants who require a visa: **20 Oct 2025 – 26 Jun 2026**. Applications close at **5pm UK time**.
- Applications accepted for applicants who do not require a visa: **20 Oct 2025 – 28 Aug 2026**. Applications close at **5pm UK time**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- A minimum of an **upper second-class UK Bachelor's degree** in a relevant discipline, such as engineering, mathematics, computer science, environmental science, human or physical geography, geology, forestry, oceanography, or physics, or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard.
- Applicants with relevant professional experience are also considered.
- The programme welcomes applications from recent graduates in engineering, architecture, physical or computational sciences, mathematics, earth sciences, physics or related fields, and from those with recent professional experience.
- For China: a **four-year bachelor's degree from a recognised Chinese higher education institution** will be considered; the required grade varies depending on the awarding university.
- For China, applicants from UCL's list of Chinese universities, which includes a selection of Project 211, Project 985, and Double First-Class universities, need for upper second-class (2:1) equivalency: **Bachelor's degree with a minimum weighted average mark of 85%**. Some programmes may require higher qualifications.
- For China, applicants from all other universities recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education need for upper second-class (2:1) equivalency: **Bachelor's degree with a minimum weighted average mark of 90%**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language level for this course is: **Level 1**. Further information can be found on UCL’s [English language requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/learning-and-living-ucl/international-students/english-language-requirements) page.
- IELTS Academic Version: **Level 1: Overall score of 6.5 and a minimum of 6.0 in each component**. Applicants may take the IELTS Academic Online test; IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted.
- TOEFL iBT: tests taken from **21 January 2026** require **Level 1: Overall score of 4.5 and 4.0 in reading, writing, speaking and listening**. Tests taken before 21 January 2026 require **Level 1: Overall score of 92 with 24/30 in reading and writing and 20/30 in speaking and listening**. TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition is accepted; TOEFL iBT MyBestScore is not acceptable. UCL’s institution code for TOEFL is **9163**.
- Cambridge English: C2 Proficiency (CPE): **Level 1: Overall score of 176 with 169 in all subtests**.
- Cambridge English: C1 Advanced (CAE): **Level 1: Overall score of 176 with 169 in all subtests**.
- Pearson Test of English (Academic): **Level 1: Overall score of 75 with a minimum of 67 in each Communicative Skill**.
- [UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses) are for international students aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL and develop the academic English and academic skills required to succeed at postgraduate level.

Program Overview.content:
Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining MSc is based in London, Bloomsbury. It gives advanced understanding of GIScience, databases, spatial analysis, data mining, analytics and related areas, and builds specialist expertise to analyse, represent, and model large and complex spatio-temporal datasets. Study mode is full-time or part-time, with a duration of 1 calendar year full-time or 2 calendar years part-time.
This specialist MSc trains students to extract insights from large amounts of data to discover patterns and knowledge from spatio-temporal data. Teaching combines theory with extensive hands-on experience across big data, including spatio-temporal analysis and computation guided by statistical and machine learning techniques, space time data, parallel computing, system design, social media analysis, text mining, and programming. Students apply their skills to real-world scenarios, creating models for social media listening, understanding weather patterns, predicting earthquakes, and determining global warming trends. The programme also includes ethical and social angles to big data, helping students understand the wider context of their work.
The programme is ideal for students who want to elevate their expertise in big data to advance in a career or go on to further research. UCL welcomes applications from recent graduates in engineering, architecture, physical or computational sciences, mathematics, earth sciences, physics or related fields, and from those with recent professional experience.
The programme offers opportunities to study alongside expert academics and researchers in data science, cybercrime, computation, infrastructure, geospatial sciences, urban simulation, machine learning, and more. It is supported by close industry and research links, including exclusive seminars and exhibitions with industry leaders at UCL. Students gain hands-on experience with data acquisition tools, software, programming languages such as R and Python, real-case data, and open-source software. UCL’s Bloomsbury campus is in the heart of a London district known for cultural and educational institutions.
Graduates from the programme have gone on to work with employers such as UBS Investment Bank, Panasonic, Datacup, and Wegaw, while others have moved into research positions at institutions including the University of Cambridge and Universidad del Azuay ([Graduate Outcomes Survey 2017-22](https://public.tableau.com/app/profile/katy.coyte4085/viz/WhatDoUCLGraduatesDo/WhatdoUCLgraduatesdo)). The programme combines theory, practice, and innovation to provide a strong technical and contextual foundation for big data careers in industry or further research.
Students have regular opportunities to connect, collaborate, and build professional contacts through guest lectures, special seminars, collaborative group projects, field trips, site visits, case studies, workshops within the department and with industry partners, and [UCL Careers](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/careers) resources and events.
The MSc is delivered through seminars, lectures, laboratory work, projects, and practicals, often drawing on real-life industry case studies with opportunities for hands-on experience. Assessment is through examinations, presentations, essays, coursework, and a research project submitted as a dissertation. Full-time students can expect 12-16 hours of contact time per teaching week, plus around 20-25 hours per week of self-directed study and assessment work; the full-time course is approximately 35-40 hours a week.
The programme consists of compulsory modules, optional modules, and a dissertation/report. Full-time students complete the structure over the MSc, part-time students over 2 years, and modular/flexible students over the course of their studies. Upon successful completion of 180 credits, students are awarded an MSc in Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining; upon successful completion of 120 credits, students are awarded a PG Dip in Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining.

Curriculum.content:
Study mode: Full-time or part-time. Duration: full-time **1 calendar year**; part-time **2 calendar years**. Programme starts September 2026.
Teaching and learning: This MSc programme is delivered through a mix of seminars, lectures, laboratory work, projects and practicals. Assessment is through examinations, presentations, essays, coursework, and a research project submitted as a dissertation. Full-time students can expect 12-16 hours of contact time per teaching week, plus around 20-25 hours per week of self-directed study and assessments. This is a full-time course, with an expected working schedule of approximately 35-40 hours a week.
Modules: Students undertake modules to the value of **180 credits**. Upon successful completion of 180 credits, students are awarded an MSc in Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining.
Programme structure:
- Full-time: total of **180 credits**; consists of 3 compulsory modules, 5 optional modules and a dissertation/report.
- Part-time: total of **180 credits over 2 years**; consists of 3 compulsory modules, 5 optional modules and a dissertation/report.
- Flexible: total of **180 credits** over the course of studies.
Compulsory modules:
- [Geospatial Science](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/geospatial-science-CEGE0094)
- [Machine Learning for Data Science](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/machine-learning-for-data-science-CEGE0004)
- [Spatial-Temporal Data Analysis and Data Mining (STDM)](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/spatial-temporal-data-analysis-and-data-mining-stdm-CEGE0042)
- [Research Project](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/research-project-CEGE0049)
- [Geospatial Programming](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/geospatial-programming-CEGE0096)
- [Spatial Analysis and Geocomputation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/spatial-analysis-and-geocomputation-CEGE0097)
Optional modules:
- Web and Mobile GIS - Apps and Programming
- [Spatial Databases and Data Management](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/spatial-databases-and-data-management-CEGE0052)
- [Sensors and Location](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/sensors-and-location-CEGE0095)
- Introduction to Complex Infrastructure Systems
- [Urban Simulation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/urban-simulation-CASA0002)
- Mining Social and Geographic Datasets
- [Cybercrime](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/cybercrime-SECU0043)
A Postgraduate Diploma, consisting of five core modules (**75 credits**) and three optional modules (**45 credits**), taken full-time over nine months is also offered. Upon successful completion of **120 credits**, students are awarded a PG Dip in Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining.

Financial Aid.content:
- **Spärck AI Scholarship**: UK Government award supporting talented leaders in AI and its application across diverse disciplines.
- **Value:** Full tuition fees plus **£22,780 stipend** for one year. UCL has **8 scholarships** to award in total, with up to 100 scholarships available across all nine participating UK universities in 2026/27.
- **Available to:** Prospective students. **Eligible fee status:** Home and Overseas. **Selection criteria:** Academic Merit; strengths and motivations, prioritizing underrepresented groups.
- **Eligible programme:** [MSc Spatio-Temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/taught-degrees/spatio-temporal-analytics-and-big-data-mining-msc), as one of the selected 1-year full-time Master's programmes.
- Eligibility requires candidates to have submitted a complete admission application, including references, for a full-time Master's degree at UCL starting in 2026/27.
- The scholarship is tenable for one year only and may not be held alongside other UK Government scholarships, studentships, awards, or bursaries. Recipients must inform the UCL Student Funding Office immediately of any other funding awarded towards their UCL Master’s degree studies.
- To apply: applicants should already have received an offer of admission from one of the participating programmes, complete the [Sparck AI Scholarship Application Form](https://view.officeapps.live.com/op/view.aspx?src=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ucl.ac.uk%2Fscholarships%2Fsites%2Fscholarships%2Ffiles%2Fsparck_ai_application_form.docx&wdOrigin=BROWSELINK), and obtain a reference letter using the [Reference Guidance - Sparck AI Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/sites/scholarships/files/sparck_ai_scholarship_reference_document.pdf).
- Completed application form and reference must be emailed for MSc Spatio-Temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining to [cege-pg-admissions@ucl.ac.uk](mailto:cege-pg-admissions@ucl.ac.uk) by **17:00 (BST), Friday 1st May 2026**.
- Results timeline: interviews for shortlisted candidates are expected in **early June 2026**; scholarship offers in **mid to late June 2026**; offers must be accepted by **mid-July 2026** at the latest. Scholarships are for study only in academic year 2026-27 and cannot be deferred.

Multiple Applications.content: Please note - you can only apply to a **maximum of two taught graduate courses in any academic cycle**.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer. However, if you need to defer for one of the reasons below, UCL will consider your request.
UCL will consider a request to defer only in the following circumstances:
- The serious illness of the offer holder or the serious illness of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The death of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The need to take parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months.
- Where the offer holder is directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster (i.e., war, earthquakes or flooding).
- The offer holder has been awarded a UCL scholarship (including UCL partnership agreements and Faculty awards); or a full scholarship (tuition fee and maintenance support) from a recognised funding body - for study in the following academic year. A “scholarship” does not include student loans.
- The offer holder holds an offer to study the **UCL International Pre-Masters**.
To be eligible for a deferral you must hold an unconditional offer which you have accepted. The exception is if you hold an offer for the International Pre-Masters, in which case an accepted conditional offer is allowed. You must also have paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt, if a deposit requirement is in place for your programme.
If you wish to defer but do not fall into one of the above categories you may apply for the next academic year once applications open, however, applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake.
To request a deferral for one of the above reasons, do so on the offer page of your application portal. If requesting a deferral due to illness or parental or adoption leave, you need to provide a letter from a relevant medical practitioner. If the request is based on a scholarship for study in the following academic year, you must upload a copy of your official scholarship award letter. UCL reserves the right to request more information before making a final decision.
An application cannot be deferred twice. Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants.
The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
If your deferral request is unsuccessful, you may apply for the next academic year once applications open, however, applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that particular intake.
If your deferral request is approved, you will receive a new offer letter and may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date. If your request to defer is approved, any tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
You must meet all your conditions and hold an unconditional offer before you can enrol.
- Your offer letter will contain information on any deadlines that apply to your offer. If circumstances mean that you will not be able to meet your offer conditions by these dates, contact the [Graduate Admissions Team](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/stay-touch/ask-admissions-postgraduate-and-teacher-training-enquiries).
- Academic degree documents: “We cannot accept anything other than **final official documents** to meet the conditions of your offer.”
- English Language conditions: If you need to take an English language test to meet your offer conditions, UCL recommends booking a test as early as possible. Official results must be provided; UCL will not accept screenshots of your results portal.
- [UCL Pre-sessional English courses](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses/pre-sessional-english-courses/pg): “You can take a Pre-sessional English course at UCL to settle the English language condition in your offer.”
- To clear offer conditions, upload documents to the applicant portal if you have an academic condition and have received degree documents and transcripts from your university. Proof of English language proficiency must also be uploaded to the applicant portal.
- If you have not met your academic offer condition, you should still upload your documents; the Admissions team will still consider whether your offer can be confirmed.
- If you have not met your English language test condition but have received scores that meet the **UCL level 1 requirement**, you can still supply your test scores to UCL for review. UCL “will not ordinarily accept a lower score than stipulated in the offer” and “cannot consider test scores that do not meet the **UCL level 1 requirement**.”
